desc:
Order and inventory sync between systems keeps stock counts and order details matching across your store, marketplace, warehouse tool and sheets. Ecom Swift LLC builds the connections, tests them with sample orders and adds alerts for gaps.

## What is order and inventory sync?

Order and inventory sync is an automated link between the systems that hold your stock and your sales. When a unit sells in one place, the count drops in the others. When a new order arrives, the details reach whoever packs and ships it. When a shipment is marked sent, the store hears about it.

Each product is matched across systems by its SKU, the code that identifies it, so the same item is recognized wherever it appears.

## Why tracking stock in two places leads to overselling

A product that exists in a web store, a marketplace and a spreadsheet has three stock numbers. They agree on the day you set them up and drift apart from then on. A sale on one channel is not seen by the others, a return is added in only one place, and a manual count is typed into the wrong tab.

The result is an order for something you do not have. You then cancel it, apologize and lose both the sale and some trust. Staff spend hours reconciling counts, and the more channels you add, the worse it becomes. A single flow of truth removes most of that work.

## How syncing affects fulfilment and customer experience

The main gain is fewer mistakes. Stock that is updated the moment something sells makes overselling far less likely, and customers see accurate availability. Orders that reach the fulfilment team automatically are packed sooner, since nobody waits for a copy-and-paste step.

Status updates sent back to the store let customers see progress and reduce questions to your support inbox. Low-stock alerts give the buyer time to reorder before a bestseller runs out. A change log means that when a number looks wrong, you can trace exactly which update changed it and when.

## What a great sync includes

- Products matched across systems by SKU, with a clean list of unmatched items.
- Stock updates in one direction or both, chosen to suit how you work.
- New orders sent to your fulfilment team or warehouse tool.
- Order status and tracking updates returned to the store.
- A change log sheet showing every update, with time and source.
- Low-stock alerts to the right person.
- A mismatch report that compares systems and flags gaps.
- A one-click pause for the sync, for stock counts or maintenance.
- Safe handling when one system is down, so changes are not lost.
- Testing with sample orders before real ones.

## How we build it

We start by mapping your systems and deciding which one is the source for stock. Then we match products by SKU and clean the list, because duplicate or missing SKUs are the most common cause of trouble. Next we build the connections, run sample orders through each route and compare the counts at every step.

Basic keeps two systems aligned in one direction with a low-stock alert. Standard connects more systems, syncs both ways, sends orders to fulfilment and records a change log. Premium covers a wider set of systems and products, sends order status back to the store, adds a mismatch report and a pause control, and tests with a larger batch of sample orders. We do not create marketplace listings as part of this work.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give each product one unique SKU everywhere.
- Choose one system as the master for stock.
- Run a full stock count before switching the sync on.
- Pause the sync during large imports or stocktakes.
- Check the change log after the first few real days.

**Avoid:**
- Editing stock by hand in several systems at once.
- Reusing a SKU for two different products.
- Syncing every field when only stock and status matter.
- Switching the sync on before products are matched.
- Ignoring mismatch reports once the system seems quiet.

## Who it is for

A seller on a store and a marketplace who is tired of canceling orders for items that sold out elsewhere. A business that uses a spreadsheet for purchasing and wants it to follow real sales. A brand that works with a separate warehouse and needs orders and tracking to flow without emails.

## What we need from you

Share the systems you use, a product export with SKUs and the name of the person who handles fulfilment. Tell us how returns and backorders should be treated. We work as a collaborator, staff or developer user in your own accounts, never ask for passwords, and leave the connections under your ownership.
